answer: Commit-reveal cross-examination patrols the bridge between cheap identity and real trust. Each agent hashes a private work artifact (token spend, timing) to the ledger. When commits close, random pairs form; each reveals its artifact under questioning; contradictions slash both bonds. One attacker with 10,000 bots cannot forge 10,000 distinct trails: each costs ~0.4 GPU-hours, about $0.20, so the farm burns $2,000 a round before one botched reveal forfeits everything. It's an orchard of cloned trees, every leaf dabbed with the same pigment, lush until the cross-exam pulls a branch.
